newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money stable at 3.05 to 3.10 percent.
newsitem.headline: German call money stable at 3.05 to 3.10 percent.

text.p: German call money rates remained steady at around 3.05 to 3.10 percent on Tuesday in what dealers described as quiet trade.
Traders said that the Bundesbank, seeking to maintain smooth dealings, was likely to steer liquidity to keep money rates in their current range for the near future.
The Bundesbank said earlier that it had set a 14-day repo tender at a fixed 3.00 percent rate. An 82.4 billion mark 3.00 percent facility expires on Wednesday.

Reserves held by commercial banks at the central bank stood at 40.3 billion marks on Monday unchanged from Friday's levels while average reserves for the month to date were 40.2 billion marks, also unchanged.
Borrowing on the Lombard facility was negligible.
In midsession trade on Tuesday, the Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average rate was quoted at 3.10567 percent, up slightly from 3.10400 percent on Monday.
